items.english: Outside the door, grown dark at some point, was the sound of hard rain and wind. A storm.

The parents and the child had gathered around the table under the dim electric light hung close to the wall of the narrow room, about to have their supper. Father and mother were both still really young. And the child was a round, plump little girl, just able to stand holding on to the table.

Neither the man nor the woman had a wrinkle yet in the face. But in the man's hollowed, kind-looking eyes in the shadow of his thick eyebrows there was a look of listless weariness. And in the color of the woman's dark hair and about her slender shoulders there was a still deeper, sunken weariness, and a drowsy peace.
The day had ended. The sorrow and suffering of that day were about to flow away into the peace of the night. And they, smiling in silence, kept all their eyes upon the child.

Standing unsteadily, the child kept trying, with fat, round hands short as balls, to sweep at the things on the table, without a moment's pause and far too fast. So, smiling, they put all the tea bowls and the teapot and the aluminum pot and the rest under the table. Left on the table were only the small spoon the child held and a single small plate.
But the child, giving a noisy little cry full of joy, banged the spoon and the plate down on the table.

data.say: Drafted the opening storm and supper tableau, keeping objects plain and weariness and smiling repeated.
